cause_summary: Low fuel-tank pressure caused loss of thrust ~2s after liftoff; vehicle fell back and exploded
lesson_learned: Early US pressurization/fuel-feed margins inadequate; pointed to need for rigorous engine start sequencing
fix_hold_evidence: Program deprioritized in favor of Army's Explorer 1; Vanguard later flew successfully (SLV) in 1958-59
primary_reference: US Navy / Naval Research Laboratory internal review (1957)

cause_summary: Second-stage engine ignited on the pad during repairs with fueled vehicle; ~78-126 killed
lesson_learned: Never work on a fueled vehicle with power to ignition systems; safety interlocks and range clearance discipline
fix_hold_evidence: Fueling-safety protocols enforced; no comparable pad-fueling catastrophe recurred in the Soviet program
primary_reference: Soviet State Commission report (Brezhnev/Ustinov commission, 1960) — classified until 1989

cause_summary: Cabin fire in 100% O2 at 16.7 psi ignited by wiring arc; hatch could not open in time
lesson_learned: Eliminate pure high-pressure O2 ground atmospheres; outward-opening quick hatch; flammable-material control
fix_hold_evidence: Pure-O2 pad atmosphere removed, outward hatch, flammables purged; no further Apollo cabin fire
primary_reference: Report of the Apollo 204 Review Board (NASA, 1967)

cause_summary: Main and reserve parachutes failed to deploy properly; capsule crashed, killing Komarov
lesson_learned: Parachute system qualification and independent redundancy; do not fly with known unresolved defects
fix_hold_evidence: Parachute system redesigned; but parachute/descent failures recurred (Soyuz 11 depressurization, 1971, killed 3)

cause_summary: 30-engine first stage plagued by pogo, plumbing fires, and KORD control shutdowns; never reached orbit
lesson_learned: Untested clustered engines at scale are high-risk; ground-test the full stage before flight
fix_hold_evidence: Program cancelled 1974; the absence of an all-up engine test stand was the cited systemic cause

cause_summary: Cold O-ring in SRB field joint failed, hot gas burned into ET; vehicle broke up at T+73s
lesson_learned: Do not launch outside qualified temperature envelope; heed engineering dissent; joint redesign
fix_hold_evidence: SRB joint/O-ring redesign held technically — but the organizational root cause (normalized deviance) recurred and caused Columbia (2003)
primary_reference: Report of the Presidential Commission on the Space Shuttle Challenger Accident (Rogers Commission, 1986)

cause_summary: Reused Ariane 4 IRS code: 64-bit float to 16-bit int overflow triggered guidance shutdown, self-destruct
lesson_learned: Requalify inherited software for new flight envelope; handle numeric exceptions; test with real trajectory data
fix_hold_evidence: Inertial-reference software requalified for the new trajectory; Ariane 5 went on to ~100+ successes
primary_reference: ARIANE 5 Flight 501 Failure — Report by the Inquiry Board (Lions Report, ESA/CNES, 1996)

cause_summary: Wrong roll-rate filter constant loaded in Centaur software; satellite stranded in useless orbit
lesson_learned: Verify flight-software constants/tables; independent load review
fix_hold_evidence: Software-constant verification and independent load review instituted; no recurrence of that Centaur load error
primary_reference: USAF / Aerospace Corp Accident Investigation Board (1999)

cause_summary: Ground software used pound-force-seconds vs newton-seconds; navigation error caused too-low orbit insertion
lesson_learned: Enforce consistent units across contractors; independent nav verification; interface control documents
fix_hold_evidence: SI units mandated and interface control enforced; no recurrence of a units-mismatch loss
primary_reference: Mars Climate Orbiter Mishap Investigation Board Phase I Report (NASA, 1999)

cause_summary: Spurious leg-deploy signal read as touchdown; engines cut off ~40m up; lander crashed
lesson_learned: Filter transient sensor signals; test full EDL software with realistic sensor noise
fix_hold_evidence: Touchdown-sensor logic corrected; later landers (Phoenix, MSL) added EDL telemetry and succeeded
primary_reference: Report on the Loss of the Mars Polar Lander and Deep Space 2 Missions (JPL/Casani Report, 2000)

cause_summary: Foam strike on ascent breached wing RCC leading edge; hot plasma destroyed orbiter on reentry
lesson_learned: Treat 'in-family' anomalies seriously; foam shedding was normalized deviance; enable on-orbit inspection/repair
fix_hold_evidence: On-orbit inspection, foam-shedding fixes, ISS safe-haven; Shuttle flew 22 more safe missions then retired (2011)
primary_reference: Columbia Accident Investigation Board (CAIB) Report, Vol. I (2003)

cause_summary: First-stage engine ingested debris (FOD); engine failed at liftoff, vehicle exploded on the pad
lesson_learned: Foreign-object-debris control in turbopump/inlet; pad-abort protection
fix_hold_evidence: Engine turbopump debris path corrected; Sea Launch returned to flight in 2008
primary_reference: Sea Launch / RSC Energia failure review (2007)

cause_summary: Residual thrust from new Merlin 1C after shutdown caused stage recontact at separation
lesson_learned: Account for engine chill/residual thrust in staging timing; SpaceX fixed and reached orbit on Flight 4
fix_hold_evidence: Stage-separation timing margin increased; Falcon 1 Flight 4 reached orbit (first private liquid-fuel orbital rocket)

cause_summary: Fregat/upper-stage propulsion anomaly stranded satellite
lesson_learned: Upper-stage reliability and restart qualification
fix_hold_evidence: Power-subsystem review conducted; on-orbit power failures remained a recurring satellite-reliability theme

cause_summary: Three angular-rate sensors installed upside-down; vehicle veered and crashed seconds after liftoff
lesson_learned: Poka-yoke (mistake-proof) sensor mounting; inspection cannot be the only barrier
fix_hold_evidence: Angular-rate sensors keyed to prevent inverted install (poka-yoke); but Proton suffered further failures in 2014 & 2015 from other causes

cause_summary: Refurbished AJ26 (NK-33) turbopump failure led to loss of thrust and explosion
lesson_learned: Aging Soviet-surplus engines carry high risk; Antares re-engined with RD-181
fix_hold_evidence: Refurbished AJ26 engines retired; Antares re-engined with RD-181 and returned to flight successfully
primary_reference: Orbital ATK Accident Investigation Board + NASA Independent Review Team (2015)

cause_summary: Faulty upper-stage strut holding a helium COPV failed, over-pressurized LOX tank, vehicle broke up
lesson_learned: Full traceability/testing of low-cost bracket suppliers; margin on struts
fix_hold_evidence: Strut supplier changed and 100% proof-tested; that strut-failure mode did not recur

cause_summary: Solid-oxygen buildup between COPV liner and overwrap in subcooled LOX ignited during fueling
lesson_learned: Understand novel subcooled-propellant/COPV interactions; changed helium loading procedures
fix_hold_evidence: COPV helium-tank design and loading procedure changed; no recurrence of the COPV ignition mode

cause_summary: IMU saturation during parachute phase corrupted altitude estimate; thrusters cut early, crashed
lesson_learned: Guard against sensor saturation propagating into nav; robust estimator design
fix_hold_evidence: IMU-saturation handling and altitude logic corrected; ExoMars rover landing (the intended follow-on) has not yet flown
primary_reference: ESA Schiaparelli Anomaly Inquiry Board Report (2017)

cause_summary: YF-77 first-stage engine turbopump anomaly; delayed China's heavy-lift and lunar plans ~2.5 years
lesson_learned: Turbopump robustness for hydrolox first stages; extensive ground re-test before return-to-flight
fix_hold_evidence: YF-77 engine turbopump redesigned; LM-5 returned to flight (2019) and launched Tianwen-1, Chang'e-5, Tiangong modules

cause_summary: Bent separation sensor pin (assembly damage) caused a strap-on booster to strike the core; crew aborted safely
lesson_learned: Assembly-induced damage detection; the abort system worked and saved the crew
fix_hold_evidence: Launch-escape system worked (crew safe); bent separation-sensor assembly-QA fixed; no recurrence

cause_summary: Thermo-structural failure in the Zefiro-23 second-stage forward dome
lesson_learned: Second-stage structural qualification under flight thermal loads
fix_hold_evidence: Zefiro-23 second-stage fix issued — but Vega failed again in 2020 (VV17, human cabling error), showing QA problems persisted

cause_summary: One of five engines shut down at ignition; vehicle slid sideways off the pad before climbing
lesson_learned: Engine-out robustness and ignition reliability for small launchers
fix_hold_evidence: Engine-shutdown/fuel-leak fixes made — but Rocket 3 failed again (TROPICS-1, 2022); Astra abandoned the vehicle

cause_summary: One engine shut down ~15s in; vehicle went transonic asymmetric, lost control, terminated
lesson_learned: First-flight engine reliability; thrust-vector authority with engine-out
fix_hold_evidence: Premature-shutdown/FTS fixes let Flight 2 reach orbit — but Alpha suffered further failures (2024, 2025)

cause_summary: Upper-stage engine shut down early; payload not delivered to orbit
lesson_learned: Upper-stage propulsion margin for small launchers
fix_hold_evidence: Upper-stage propellant/injector fix issued, but Astra retired Rocket 3 entirely; NASA lost 2 TROPICS cubesats

cause_summary: Simultaneous engine shutdown from a power-system fire/electrical fault; vehicle fell back
lesson_learned: Harden avionics power and fire protection in the engine bay
fix_hold_evidence: Engine-fire/power-loss fixes issued, but ABL later exited the orbital-launch business
primary_reference: ABL Space Systems internal investigation, FAA-overseen (2023)

cause_summary: Second-stage LE-5B ignition failed after an electrical/signal fault detected excess current
lesson_learned: Upper-stage ignition electrical fault isolation and requalification
fix_hold_evidence: Second-stage ignition electrical fault fixed; H3 TF2 succeeded (2024) and H3 became operational

cause_summary: Multiple Raptor engine failures, loss of thrust-vector control; pad destroyed by lack of flame diverter
lesson_learned: Add flame deflector/water deluge; improve Raptor reliability and stage separation approach
fix_hold_evidence: Water-cooled steel deluge plate, hot-stage ring, FTS upgrades; corrections validated on later flights

cause_summary: Propellant leak from a ruptured oxidizer tank/valve prevented lunar landing attempt
lesson_learned: Propulsion valve/tank qualification for commercial landers; propellant system redundancy
fix_hold_evidence: Astrobotic's next lander (Griffin Mission One) is scheduled no earlier than Nov 2026

cause_summary: Ship lost attitude control (clogged RCS) and broke up on reentry; booster lost before splashdown
lesson_learned: Roll-control/RCS reliability; reentry thermal and attitude management
fix_hold_evidence: Attitude-control and reentry thermal fixes; reached near-orbital velocity — data-gathering test flight

cause_summary: Stage separation anomaly damaged upper-stage engine nozzle; payload placed in too-low orbit and reentered
lesson_learned: Separation dynamics and nozzle protection during staging
fix_hold_evidence: Stage-separation collision fix issued — but Alpha failed again in 2025 (FLTA006), indicating unresolved reliability

cause_summary: Harmonic/vibration response drove propellant-line leaks and fires in the ship's aft; vehicle lost over Atlantic
lesson_learned: Address POGO/harmonic coupling in new V2 ship; propellant-line robustness
fix_hold_evidence: Propellant-line harmonic/vibration fix issued — but the upper stage failed again on Flight 8, the same basic loss

cause_summary: Hardware failure in a center Raptor led to loss of the ship again; debris over Caribbean
lesson_learned: Repeat aft-section reliability issue; design changes to Raptor and aft thermal protection
fix_hold_evidence: Engine-hardware fix after repeat upper-stage loss; booster caught successfully — V2 issues addressed on V3

cause_summary: Stage-separation anomaly / nozzle loss reduced upper-stage performance; payload lost
lesson_learned: Recurring staging/nozzle issue points to design margin, not one-off
fix_hold_evidence: Return-to-flight 'Stairway To Seven' (12 Mar 2026) reached orbit

cause_summary: Third-stage (solid) pressure anomaly caused loss of the mission
lesson_learned: Solid-motor case/nozzle margin; rare PSLV failure prompts review
fix_hold_evidence: PSLV-C62 (12 Jan 2026) failed in the same third-stage phase eight months later; ISRO's FAC report (13 Jun 2026) was not made public

cause_summary: A COPV in the payload bay failed during fueling for a static fire; ship destroyed on test stand
lesson_learned: Composite pressure-vessel handling and inspection; ground-test hazard control
fix_hold_evidence: Starship flew Flights 12-14 (May-Sep 2026) with no recurrence of the COPV failure reported

cause_summary: Upper-stage anomaly left a navigation satellite in an incorrect orbit
lesson_learned: Upper-stage restart/deployment reliability
fix_hold_evidence: H3 flew successfully on 12 Jun 2026 (F6) and 10 Aug 2026 (F9)

cause_summary: Roll-rate deviation near end of third-stage (PS3) burn, just before separation; 15 of 16 payloads lost (KID capsule transmitted data)
lesson_learned: Same flight regime as PSLV-C61 eight months earlier; cause report withheld, so the lesson is not shareable
fix_hold_evidence: No flight of this vehicle between the failure and 2026-10-09

cause_summary: Launch failure; Shijian 32 not delivered to geosynchronous orbit. No cause released
lesson_learned: No public cause statement
fix_hold_evidence: 2 of 2 subsequent 2026 flights succeeded (to 2026-10-09)

cause_summary: Maiden flight failed to reach orbit; 6 payloads lost. No cause released
lesson_learned: No public cause statement
fix_hold_evidence: No flight of this vehicle between the failure and 2026-10-09

cause_summary: Flight termination ~70 s after liftoff; third failure in three KAIROS flights (Mar 2024, Dec 2024, Mar 2026)
lesson_learned: Three consecutive failures of a new vehicle; causes of each not shared in a comparable public format
fix_hold_evidence: No flight of this vehicle between the failure and 2026-10-09

cause_summary: Anomaly shortly after liftoff on maiden flight. Precedent: on 30 Jun 2024 a Tianlong-3 first stage broke free of its test stand during a static fire (structural failure)
lesson_learned: No public cause statement
fix_hold_evidence: No flight of this vehicle between the failure and 2026-10-09

cause_summary: Upper stage placed BlueBird 7 in a lower-than-planned orbit; satellite could not raise orbit and was deorbited. First flight of a reused New Glenn booster
lesson_learned: Upper-stage performance shortfall; FAA mishap investigation opened, findings not public at compilation
fix_hold_evidence: No flight of this vehicle between the failure and 2026-10-09

cause_summary: Vehicle exploded during static fire; first stage and fuelled second stage destroyed, Launch Complex 36 severely damaged. Cause attributed (5 Aug 2026) to a BE-4 main oxygen valve
lesson_learned: Third pad-loss during a fuelled test in a decade (AMOS-6 2016, Starship Ship 36 2025): ground tests need flight-level hazard controls
fix_hold_evidence: No flight of this vehicle between the failure and 2026-10-09
primary_reference: Blue Origin statement on cause, 5 Aug 2026

cause_summary: Vehicle disintegrated ~85 s after liftoff, around maximum dynamic pressure; ChinaSat-4B lost
lesson_learned: No public cause statement
fix_hold_evidence: No flight of this vehicle between the failure and 2026-10-09
